reference: GNU coreutils cp invoked by system Bash with its standard executable PATH; expected command status, output bytes, and file tree are compared against the bash-os cp builtin.
coverage: Binary regular-file copy, source preservation, and verbose output
Multiple operands into an existing directory, including a leading-dash name after --
Recursive tree copy with a relative symlink
Archive copy preserving hard-link relationships, symlinks, and modes
Default following of a destination symlink including -f following an openable referent
Same-file and missing-source diagnostics with unchanged fixture data
Interactive overwrite acceptance and decline using bounded here-string input
Bash type/help metadata contract for the registered cp builtin
Additional bounded regular-file, hardlink, symlink and multi-operand error continuation regressions.
exclusions: Device nodes, FIFOs, sockets, ACLs, extended attributes, and security labels are outside this private regular-file/symlink fixture suite.
The suite does not claim full GNU option coverage or compare timestamps because the harness tree snapshot records contents, modes, and link relationships but not timestamps.

cases.purpose: Copies deterministic binary data, leaves the source intact, and compares GNU-compatible -v output.
cases.script:
printf 'head\000middle\377tail\n' > source
if cp -v source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]
printf 'cp-status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Copies multiple files into an existing directory and honors -- before a source whose name begins with a dash.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'dash-name\n' > ./-first
printf 'second\n' > second
if cp -- -first second destination; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Copies a nested directory recursively and preserves a relative symlink as a symlink.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub
printf 'nested payload\n' > source/sub/item
ln -s sub/item source/shortcut
if cp -R source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Checks -a over a directory containing a hard-linked pair and a symlink; the tree comparison includes modes and hard-link identity.
cases.script:
mkdir source
printf 'shared bytes\n' > source/one
ln source/one source/two
ln -s one source/shortcut
if cp -a source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Uses a controlled umask to make a 0640 source and verifies that -p preserves its mode and bytes.
cases.script:
umask 027
printf 'mode payload\n' > source
umask 022
if cp -p source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Verifies -f does not override -n in either option order and checks the documented --no-clobber spelling.
cases.script:
printf 'new data\n' > source
printf 'first old\n' > first
printf 'second old\n' > second
printf 'third old\n' > third
if cp -fn source first && cp -nf source second && cp --no-clobber source third; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Checks the default behavior when a regular-file destination is a symlink: the target contents change and the symlink remains.
cases.script:
printf 'replacement\n' > source
printf 'old target\n' > target
ln -s target alias
if cp source alias; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: GNU cp -f follows an openable destination symlink and writes its referent while preserving the symlink.
cases.script:
printf 'replacement\n' > source
printf 'old target\n' > target
ln -s target alias
if cp -f source alias; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Captures same-file and missing-source failures and verifies that both the source and an existing destination remain unchanged; diagnostic wording may vary.
cases.script:
printf 'keep these bytes\n' > source
printf 'keep destination\n' > destination
if cp source source; then same_status=0; else same_status=$?; fi
if cp absent destination; then missing_status=0; else missing_status=$?; fi
printf 'same=%s missing=%s\n' "$same_status" "$missing_status"
[[ $same_status -eq 1 && $missing_status -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Exercises -i with deterministic no and yes answers; output and the resulting files are compared with GNU cp.
cases.script:
printf 'new data\n' > source
printf 'keep on decline\n' > declined
printf 'old before accept\n' > accepted
if cp -i source declined <<< n; then declined_status=0; else declined_status=$?; fi
if cp -i source accepted <<< y; then accepted_status=0; else accepted_status=$?; fi
printf 'declined-status=%s accepted-status=%s\n' "$declined_status" "$accepted_status"

cases.purpose: Checks Bash metadata only: cp is registered as a builtin and help exposes the documented synopsis. This does not count as cp operation coverage.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t cp) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help_text=$(help cp) || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *'Copy files and directories.'* && $help_text == *'bashcp [-afinpRrv] [-HLP] SOURCE... DEST'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'type=builtin\nhelp=cp synopsis present\n'

cases.purpose: GNU cp can write regular-file data to special destinations, but this suite is restricted to relative private fixture paths.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a synthetic writable special-file sink and isolated reader, or a reviewed syscall mock. This runner must not exercise host or raw device paths.

cases.purpose: Force should write an openable destination inode, preserving its other hardlinks and existing mode.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
chmod 600 target
ln target alias
cp -f source target

cases.purpose: A forced destination symlink to the source must fail without replacing either entry.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln -s source alias
cp -f source alias

cases.purpose: Both ordinary and forced copy should reject a dangling destination symlink without creating its target.
cases.script:
printf new > source
ln -s absent alias
if cp source alias; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if cp -f source alias; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"
[[ $a == 1 && $b == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: An unwritable destination is replaced after its write-open fails; its old hardlink keeps its data.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
ln target alias
chmod 400 target
cp -f source target

cases.purpose: Check source-read failure before forced replacement for regular and symlink destinations; restore source mode for snapshots.
cases.script:
printf secret > source
printf old > target
ln -s target alias
chmod 000 source
if cp -f source target; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if cp -f source alias; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
chmod 600 source
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"
[[ $a == 1 && $b == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: A missing middle operand must not prevent the later regular file from being copied.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf first > first
printf last > last
cp first absent last destination

cases.purpose: Compare default, -P, -H, and -L copying of a command-line source symlink using GNU as the oracle.
cases.script:
printf data > source
ln -s source alias
cp alias ordinary
cp -P alias physical
cp -H alias args
cp -L alias logical

cases.purpose: Reject copying between hardlink aliases while no-clobber still skips them successfully.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln source alias
if cp -f source alias; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
cp -n source alias
printf '%s\n' "$a"
[[ $a == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: If opening the destination referent fails, force may replace the symlink after the source is readable; its old referent stays intact.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
chmod 400 target
ln -s target alias
cp -f source alias

cases.purpose: Preserve archive behavior on preexisting hardlinked destinations, with and without force.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > first
ln first first-alias
printf old > second
ln second second-alias
cp -a source first
cp -af source second
